result.summary: Philopoemen forces Sparta into the Achaean League, refuses a gift, and later reshapes Spartan institutions. Opposing Roman-leaning policy, he is captured in a fight with Messenia and poisoned, and Lycortas avenges him.

scenes.title: Philopoemen and Sparta
scenes.summary: Philopoemen brings Sparta into the Achaean League, shuts the gates against Flaminius and Diophanes, declines Nabis's house, and later exiles and sells Spartans and ends the Lycurgan training.
scenes.stakes: Sparta's independence and institutions are at stake; Philopoemen risks the Romans' and Spartans' hostility.

scenes.title: Resisting Rome's favor
scenes.summary: After Antiochus is beaten at Thermopylae, Philopoemen rebukes Aristaenus for appeasing Rome and opposes receiving Spartan exiles, then lets them return.
scenes.stakes: Greek freedom is endangered by submission to Rome.

scenes.title: Capture and death of Philopoemen
scenes.summary: Ill and over seventy, Philopoemen joins a raid on Messenia, is wounded and captured, and Dinocrates poisons him. Lycortas marches on Messene, executes the culprits, and the Arcadians bring his remains home.
scenes.stakes: Philopoemen's life is at stake; later Messene faces vengeance.

alias_notes.explanation: The Roman consul who defeated Antiochus at Thermopylae in 191 BC.

notable_quotes.reason: The popular party calls Philopoemen the father of all Greece, showing his esteem.

analysis.text: Philopoemen's career shows pride, patriotism and refusal of bribes, ending in a tragic death through civil strife.
The passage records Achaean League politics under growing Roman dominance in the early second century BC.

language_notes.text: A talent was a large weight of silver; 100 talents was a very great fortune, so the offer was lavish.
"A soul above money" means he was too high-minded to be bought; his reply redirects the bribe toward men who influenced Achaean politics.
Helots were the Spartans' state-owned serfs, mostly of Messenian or Laconian origin.
"Twitted" means taunted or reproached; "targeteers" were light infantry carrying small shields (targets).
"Fraternized" here means joined forces with Lycortas's army; "privy to" means secretly involved in.

context_notes.text: Titus Flaminius defeated Philip V of Macedon in 197 BC and proclaimed Greek freedom; Rome's power in Greece was growing.
Lycurgus was Sparta's legendary lawgiver; the training (agoge) was the harsh state education of Spartan boys. Ending it was a severe blow to Spartan identity.
Antiochus III of Syria was defeated by the Romans at Thermopylæ in 191 BC.

literary_notes.text: "A soul above money" pictures his character as rising over wealth, portraying his incorruptibility.
The narrator announces coming retribution, preparing the reader for Philopoemen's capture and death and framing it as punishment for pride.
Calling him "father of all Greece" expresses the popular esteem for Philopoemen and heightens the pathos of his murder.
